newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most active shares up in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Most active shares up in Beirut.

text.p: Most active shares rose in lower turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Thursday.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.55 percent to 193.35 and both LISPI and BLOM general indices rose 0.57 percent and 0.23 percent to 96.87 and 1113.27 respectively.
BSE turnover fell to 169,103 shares from 232,148 shares a day earlier for a value of $1,367,621 against $1,989,985.
Solidere A shares rose to $13 from $12.875 and B shares fell to $13.125 from $13.25.
Trade in the shares of Lebanon's biggest company rose to 74,293 shares from 58,230 shares.
Two out of three listed banks rose.
Banque Audi held steady at $27.125 while Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $21 from $20.5 and Bank of Beirut shares rose to $5.75 from $5.625.

Pipemaker Eternit traded at $1.90625 from $1.875 on Wednesday. A bloc of 25,000 shares traded on the BSE board at $1.875 down from $2, the price at which a bloc of 100,000 shares changed hands a day earlier.
There was no trade in the other listed industrial firms -- Ciments Blancs and and Uniceramic.
